{"parentUuid":"70714869-66f5-4c91-bf7e-53668495aa52","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["claude.ai Claude Docs"],"addedBlocks":["## claude.ai Claude Docs\nClaude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {\"kind\":\"project\",\"create\":{\"name\":\"<title>\",\"doc\":{\"blocks\":{\"asof\":{\"type\":\"date\",\"value\":\"<today>\"},\"me\":{\"type\":\"mention\",\"user\":\"me\"},\"s1\":{\"type\":\"pending\",\"intent\":\"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to\"},\"s2\":{…}},\"markdown\":\"# <title>\\n\\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\\n\\n<?claude block s1?>\\n\\n<?claude block s2?>\"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. {"parentUuid":"3e5e2586-ec85-4493-a11c-41a1c61ec420","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like \"how do I do X\", \"find a skill for X\", \"is there a skill that can...\", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.\n- mattpocock-skills:diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says \"diagnose\"/\"debug this\", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.\n- mattpocock-skills:tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions \"red-green-refactor\", or wants integration tests.\n- mattpocock-skills:prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.\n- mattpocock-skills:research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.\n- mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.\n- mattpocock-skills:codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.\n- mattpocock-skills:code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\".\n- mattpocock-skills:resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.\n- mattpocock-skills:wizard: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.\n- mattpocock-skills:grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.\n- mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.\n- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch\n- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or \"your own browser\"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for \"computer use\". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.\n- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.\n- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.\n- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.\n- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even \"change it\" or \"add a tab\". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.\n- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.\n- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.\n- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.\n- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like \"the xlsx in my downloads\") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. {"parentUuid":"ab1610d2-b0df-4d5b-a805-81984deca7a2","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"bb533be9-90e1-430c-9200-1bb5bd6b34b3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Paf6bKJnxAwz7ZnF3cPqfd","type":"tool_result","content":"author:\tyawoppongkrampah-hub\nassociation:\towner\nedited:\tfalse\nstatus:\tnone\n--\n## Follow-up from T01 (#2, commit 0cf7d23) — review before the demo release\n\n1. **Public fallback `CMS_SECRET_KEY`.** `app/settings.py` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"` when the variable is unset, so session cookies would be signed with a key that is in the repo. Decide whether the app should refuse to start (or warn loudly) without a real key.\n2. **Well-known demo passwords in `.env.example`.** `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=change-me-editor` pass the 8-character minimum, so `cms create-admin` and `scripts/seed_demo.py` will create accounts with those passwords if `.env` is copied unchanged. Consider rejecting the placeholder values, and make the release checklist say to change them.\n3. **Known limitation to review: replayed session cookies.** Sessions are stateless signed cookies (as the spec says). A copied cookie stays valid after sign-out until it expires (8 hours) or the account is Deactivated. Decide whether to accept this for the class demo and document it, or add a server-side session record.\n\nRecorded in the T01 review comment: https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/2#issuecomment-5882530574\n--\nauthor:\tyawoppongkrampah-hub\nassociation:\towner\nedited:\tfalse\nstatus:\tnone\n--\n## Follow-up from T04 (#5, commit e0df28a) — review with the session-security items above\n\n**Password reset does not end live sessions.** When an Admin sets a new password, that account's existing signed-cookie sessions stay valid until they expire (8 hours) or the account is Deactivated. #5 only requires sessions to stop on deactivation, so this was left as is (noted in the T04 review: https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/5#issuecomment-6117667918).\n\nThis is the same root cause as item 3 of the T01 follow-up (stateless signed cookies, no server-side session record). Review them together and decide either to:\n- accept it for the class demo and document it in the release checklist, or\n- add a server-side session record, or a per-account session version checked in `security.current_user`, so a reset (and a sign-out) invalidates existing sessions.\n--\n# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\n## Content\n\n**Post**\nA dated piece of writing with a title, a Markdown body, a status, an author and timestamps. Posts are for things that need to go out quickly.\n\n**Slug**\nThe URL-safe form of a title, such as `afrobeat-night`. A Post's slug is generated from its title on the first save, with a number added if it already exists. Editors never enter it. It does not change when the title or event details are corrected, so shared links keep working. Only the Admin may change a slug, and is warned that this can break an old link. A Page's slug is also Admin-only.\n\n**Event announcement**\nA Post that announces an event, such as the Afrobeat event. It has no event-date field of its own. The event's date, time, location and who can attend are written clearly in the body. _Avoid_: \"Event\" as a separate kind of content.\n\n**Announcements**\nThe public list of Published Posts, ordered by First-published date, newest first. The Home page shows the five most recent, with a link to the full list. It is not \"Upcoming Events\": newest Posts are not necessarily future events. _Avoid_: \"Upcoming Events\" for this list.\n\n**First-published date**\nThe date a Post was first Published. Announcements are ordered by it, newest first, and each Event card shows it. It is kept if the Post is unpublished and later Published again. It is never labeled as the event's date: the event's actual date and time stay in the Body.\n\n**Updated date**\nShown on an Event card when a Post's content changes after it was first Published, so visitors can tell details were corrected. Editing does not reorder the Announcements list.\n\n**Page**\nPermanent content, such as information about ASA and cultural resources. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. This is a testable vertical slice (route, template and tests) as well as the demo, screenshots and documentation tasks. It must not be completed as documentation alone.\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n**Preview and hint (route, template, tests)**\\n\\n- [ ] The Post editor and the Page editor each have a Preview that shows exactly the content the public page will render, using the same rendering and sanitizing as the export. Raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms do not run in the Preview.\\n- [ ] The Post editor shows a short Event details hint (What, When, Where, Who can attend). The hint is never pre-filled into the Body, and an Editor can hide it without deleting any content.\\n- [ ] Tests at the admin HTTP seam cover: Preview output matches the published-site output for the same Body (including sanitizing and an image with alt text); the hint appears in the Post editor, is not in the Body, and hiding it leaves the Body unchanged; and an Editor's Preview cannot be used to reach an Admin-only action.\\n\\n**Demo-ready and documented**\\n\\n- [ ] The demo seed rebuilds cleanly from `.env.example`: both roles, Published and Draft Posts and Pages, and one Deactivated account. It contains no real personal data and no claims about ASA beyond the brief.\\n- [ ] A clean-clone smoke test runs the setup from `.env.example` plus the documented steps and reaches a working sign-in. No password, `.env` or database file is committed.\\n- [ ] A release checklist covers `cms publish`, `cms deploy`, the relative-path check, adding approved image files, confirming Photo permission before a real photo is added, and the limit that an Editor cannot add an image file alone. It says that for the class demo the project author runs it, and does not claim ASA has an existing owner for this step or an approval process.\\n- [ ] The README has Live URL, Run locally and Generative AI Use Statement sections, with the Backends used table.\\n- [ ] Screenshots of the six admin screens (sign-in, dashboard, Content list, editor, users, and the permission-refusal page) at 1280 px and 390 px are saved in the screenshots folder.\\n- [ ] The Stage 2 submission checker passes.\\n\\n## Blocked by\\n\\n- #5 (T04: blocking)\\n- #7 (T06: blocking)\\n- #8 (T07: Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping {"parentUuid":"8b5d3fb8-a52d-4945-b51c-a388bc6f0f1a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"bb533be9-90e1-430c-9200-1bb5bd6b34b3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Vmy64CX9Uva9VxpYb7zugh","type":"tool_result","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nASA, the African Student Association at Kenyon, is described in the client brief as a student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. Students need an easy way to find event announcements (including an Afrobeat event), learn about the association, explore cultural resources, and see photos from past activities. Its leaders need event announcements to be quick to publish, information about ASA to stay easy to find in the navigation, and a way to share photos only when ASA has permission to use them. One ASA leader should manage accounts and permanent pages; another member should be able to write and update event posts without a complicated form.\n\nThis is a class project (IPHS 400, Mini-Project #2). No claim is made about any real ASA process, officers, schedule or history. Terms below are defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS. A local admin console lets an Admin and Editors write **Posts** and **Pages**, manage accounts, and preview content. A `cms publish` step renders only **Published** content into a static public site, and `cms deploy` sends it to GitHub Pages, at which point the content is **Live**. The admin console never goes on the public internet (ADR-001).\n\nThe public site has a **Home page** (a short **Welcome text** taken from the client brief plus the five latest **Announcements**), an **Announcements** list, and **Navigation** built from published Pages (starter Pages for the demo: About ASA, Resources, Photos). Event announcements are ordinary Posts with the event's date, time, location and who can attend written in the **Body**. Photos are images inside Posts or Pages; there is no upload form.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Signing in\n1. As an Admin, I want to sign in with a username and password, so that only authorised people can change the site.\n2. As an Editor, I want to sign in and out, so that my session ends when I leave a shared computer.\n3. As an account owner, I want my password stored hashed, so that nobody, including the Admin, can read it.\n4. As an Admin, I want a wrong password to be rejected with a clear message that does not reveal whether the username exists, so that accounts cannot be guessed.\n5. As someone with a Deactivated account, I want sign-in to be refused, so that a former member can no longer change the site.\n6. As a signed-in user, I want every form I submit to be protected against forged requests, so that another website cannot act as me.\n7. As a visitor who is not signed in, I want any admin address to send me to sign-in, so that I never see admin content.\n\n### First Admin and setup\n8. As the project owner, I want the first Admin account created from the command line with a password taken from the environment, so that no password is committed to Git.\n9. As the project owner, I want a clean clone to run from `.env.example` plus a few documented steps, so that a grader can reproduce the demo.\n10. As the project owner, I want the database and `.env` kept out of Git, so that private data is never published.\n11. As the project owner, I want demo data that can be rebuilt on demand, so that screenshots and tests are repeatable.\n\n### Roles and permission refusal\n12. As an Admin, I want to manage accounts and permanent Pages, so that I control who can change the site and what the Navigation contains.\n13. As an Editor, I want to create and publish Posts directly, so that an announcement can go out quickly.\n14. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post, including another Editor's, so that event details can be corrected close to the event if the writer is unavailable.\n15. As an Editor, I want to update the Body of an existing Page, so that the Photos page can stay current.\n16. As an Admin, I want only Admins to delete Posts, so that a mistaken deletion is unlikely.\n17. As an Admin, I want only Admins to create, delete, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug a Page, so that Navigation and links stay stable.\n18. As an Admin, I want only Admins to change a slug, and to be warned that doing so can break an old link, so that shared links keep working.\n19. As an Editor, I want admin-only controls hidden from my screens, so that my screens stay simple.\n20. As an Editor who reaches an Admin-only address or submits a forbidden action directly, I want a clear \"You don't have permission\" page with a link back to the dashboard, so that I understand what happened.\n21. As an Admin, I want every permission enforced by the server, not by hidden buttons, so that access control is real.\n\n### Posts\n22. As an Editor, I want to write a Post with a title and a Body and save it as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it is ready for the public site.\n24. As an Editor, I want to unpublish a Post, so that a wrong announcement stops going out.\n25. As an Editor, I want the slug generated from my title on first save, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n26. As an Editor, I want a number added automatically when a slug already exists, so that two Posts never collide.\n27. As an Editor, I want the slug to stay unchanged when I correct the title or event details, so that shared links keep working.\n28. As an Editor, I want a short hint reminding me to include What, When, Where and Who can attend, so that announcements are complete.\n29. As an Editor, I want the hint not pre-filled into the Body and hideable without losing content, so that I can write naturally.\n30. As an Editor, I want the Post to record me as its Author automatically, so that I do not fill in extra fields.\n31. As an Editor, I want the Post's created, updated and first-published times recorded automatically, so that dates are trustworthy.\n\n### Pages\n32. As an Admin, I want to create a Page with a title, slug and Body, so that permanent information has a home.\n33. As an Admin, I want a published Page to appear in the public Navigation automatically, so that visitors can find it.\n34. As an Admin, I want an unpublished Page to disappear from the Navigation, so that unfinished pages are not linked.\n35. As an Admin, I want to delete a Page, so that obsolete pages can be removed.\n36. As an Editor, I want to edit the Body of a Page but see title, slug, status and delete controls as unavailable, so that I cannot break the Navigation.\n\n### Writing, preview and images\n37. As an Editor, I want to use headings, emphasis, lists, links and images with alt text, so that announcements read well without learning HTML.\n38. As an Editor, I want raw HTML, scripts, frames and forms in my text stripped, so that the site is safe.\n39. As an Editor, I want a preview that shows exactly what the public page will render, so that there are no surprises after publishing.\n40. As an Editor, I want to write a caption, alt text and Markdown reference for an image, so that photos are accessible.\n41. As an Editor, I understand I cannot add a new image file myself, so that the release-holder can confirm Photo permission first.\n42. As the release-holder, I want approved image files copied into the public site with relative paths, so that photos show up after deployment.\n43. As the release-holder, I want demo illustrations labelled as illustrative and never presented as photos of real ASA events, so that visitors are not misled.\n\n### Admin console\n44. As an Admin, I want a dashboard with the counts of Published Posts, Draft Posts, Published Pages and Draft Pages, so that I see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As an Admin, I want the dashboard to also show the number of active and Deactivated accounts, so that I can keep track of who has access.\n46. As an Editor, I want the dashboard to show the four content counts but no account counts, so that I only see what I need.\n47. As any signed-in user, I want a reminder on the dashboard that marking content Published does not make it Live until `cms publish` and `cms deploy` run, so that I do not expect instant changes.\n48. As any signed-in user, I want one Content list I can filter by Post or Page and by Draft or Published, so that I can find content without opening each item.\n49. As any signed-in user, I want each row to show title, status, Display name and last-updated time, so that I can tell items apart.\n50. As a phone user, I want the admin console usable at phone width, so that I can post from anywhere.\n\n### User management\n51. As an Admin, I want to create an account with a username, a private password, a role and a public Display name, so that a new member can start writing.\n52. As an Admin, I want to change an account's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n53. As an Admin, I want to deactivate an account, so that a former member can no longer sign in while their published Posts stay.\n54. As an Admin, I want to reactivate a deactivated account, so that a mistake is recoverable.\n55. As an Admin, I want to set a new password for an existing account without seeing the old one, so that a lost password can be recovered.\n56. As an Admin, I want a reset password never printed or logged, so that it cannot leak.\n57. As an Admin, I want to change an account's Display name, so that a former member can ask for their name to be replaced with \"ASA Events Team\".\n58. As an Admin, I want the original Author link of every Post kept, even after a Display name change or deactivation, so that the record stays accurate.\n59. As an Admin, I want the private username never used as a byline by default, so that private account names do not appear publicly.\n60. As an Admin, I want accounts deactivated rather than deleted, so that history is preserved.\n\n### Public site\n61. As a first-time visitor, I want a short welcome on the Home page, so that I know what ASA is and that I am welcome.\n62. As a visitor, I want the five latest Announcements on the Home page with a link to all of them, so that I can see what is new.\n63. As a visitor, I want an Announcements page listing all Published Posts, newest first by first-published date, so that I can browse.\n64. As a visitor, I want each Announcement as a clear Event card showing its title, first-published date and byline, so that I can scan quickly on a phone.\n65. As a visitor, I want an \"Updated\" date on a card when the content changed after first publishing, so that I know details were corrected.\n66. As a visitor, I want the event's actual date, time, location and who can attend in the Body, and the publication date never labelled as the event date, so that I am not misled.\n67. As a visitor, I want a Post to keep its original first-published date if it is unpublished and later published again, so that the order is stable.\n68. As a visitor, I want the Navigation to list Announcements and every published Page (About ASA, Resources, Photos for the demo), so that information is easy to find.\n69. As a visitor, I want the Photos page to say that actual event photos will be added when ASA has permission to use them, so that placeholders are not mistaken for real events.\n70. As a visitor, I want the public site to work on a phone with readable text, so that I can use it anywhere.\n71. As a visitor who uses a keyboard or screen reader, I want a sensible heading order, readable contrast, visible focus, keyboard access to all controls, and alt text on every image, so that the site is accessible.\n72. As a visitor, I want Drafts and unpublished content never to appear anywhere in the public site, so that unfinished work stays private.\n73. As a visitor, I want the site to work from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no link or style is broken.\n\n### Releasing\n74. As the release-holder, I want `cms publish` to write the public site from Published content only, so that Drafts never leave the database.\n75. As the release-holder, I want `cms deploy` to send the result to GitHub Pages, so that content becomes Live.\n76. As the release-holder, I want a short release checklist covering publish, deploy, checking relative paths, adding approved images, and confirming Photo permission, so that the step is quick and repeatable.\n77. As the release-holder, I want the checklist to state that an Editor cannot add an image file alone, so that clients are not surprised.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture is fixed** by ADR-001 (local admin console, static public site) and ADR-002 (FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, argon2, Markdown sanitizer). No new dependencies.\n- **Content model.** Two kinds of content only: Post and Page. No separate Event type and no event-date field. A Post has a title, slug, Markdown Body, status (Draft or Published), Author, and created, updated and first-published times. A Page has the same fields except that the Author is optional for display and a Page does not appear in the Announcements list.\n- **First-published date** is set the first time a Post becomes Published and never cleared, including when the Post is unpublished and republished. The **Updated date** on the public card is shown when the Body or title changes after the first-published date.\n- **Ordering.** Announcements are ordered by first-published date, newest first. Editing does not reorder. The Home page shows the five most recent; the Announcements page shows all Published Posts.\n- **Slugs.** A Post's slug is generated from its title on first save, made unique by adding a number, and never changed automatically. A Page's slug is entered by the Admin. Only the Admin can change any slug, and the form warns that this can break existing links. Slug edits are not shown to Editors.\n- **Accounts.** An account has a private username, a password hash, a role (Admin or Editor), a public Display name, and an active flag. There is no account deletion. Posts keep their Author link permanently. A Post's public byline is the Author's current Display name. The username is never used as a byline.\n- **Authentication.** Session cookie signed by the server. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and are never stored, shown or logged in plain form. Sign-in failures use one generic message. A Deactivated account cannot sign in and any existing session for it stops working.\n- **Authorization.** A single central rule table maps each action to the roles allowed. Every state-changing route checks it on the server. Templates hide controls the current role cannot use, but hiding is never the protection. A refused action shows a \"You don't have permission\" page with a link to the dashboard, and a not-signed-in visitor is sent to sign-in.\n- **Permission matrix.** Admin: everything. Editor: sign in and out; create, edit and publish or unpublish Posts, including other people's; edit the Body of an existing Page; view dashboard counts and the Content list. Editor cannot: delete Posts or Pages; create, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug Pages; change any slug; open user management or change any account, role or Display name; reset passwords.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies.\n- **Markdown and sanitizing.** Allowed: headings, emphasis, lists, links and images with alt text. Raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms are stripped. The same rendering and sanitizing path is used for the admin preview and the public export, so the preview matches the public page.\n- **Images.** No upload feature. Approved image files are added to the project by the release-holder and copied into the public site by `cms publish`. Markdown references use relative paths. Demo illustrations are clearly labelled illustrative.\n- **Admin console screens.** Sign-in, Dashboard, Content list, Post editor with Preview and the Event details hint, Page editor (reduced controls for Editors), User management (Admin only), and the permission-refusal page. Layouts work at phone width.\n- **Dashboard.** Four content counts for everyone; active and deactivated account counts for the Admin only; a reminder that Published is not Live. No \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- **Content list.** One list of Posts and Pages, filterable by type and by status, with title, status, Display name and last-updated time on each row.\n- **Event details hint.** A short, dismissible hint near the Post editor listing What, When, Where and Who can attend. It is never inserted into the Body.\n- **Publishing.** `cms publish` renders Home, Announcements, each Published Post, each Published Page and the Navigation to plain HTML, using only Published content and only relative paths. It copies approved image files. `cms deploy` pushes the result to the `gh-pages` branch. Nothing is Live until both have run.\n- **Public design.** Polished, mobile-first, readable text, clear Event cards, a few appropriately licensed images or decorative graphics that are never presented as real ASA event photos. Accessibility requirements: sensible heading order, readable contrast, visible focus and full keyboard access, phone-width layout, and alt text on every image.\n- **Content carried from the client brief.** The Welcome text uses only the brief's wording. Starter Pages (About ASA, Resources, Photos) and seed Posts are demo placeholders and contain no claims about ASA's real history, officers, members, schedule or approval process.\n- **First Admin.** Created from the command line at setup, with the password read from the environment. No password, `.env` or database file is committed. A clean clone runs from `.env.example` plus documented steps.\n- **Demo data.** The seed data is rebuilt on demand and includes both roles, published and draft Posts and Pages, and a deactivated account.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a signed-in user sees and can do, and what files the publish step writes. It does not check internal functions, the database layout or template details.\n- **Seam 1: the admin console over HTTP.** Use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. Cover sign-in and sign-out, Deactivated accounts, each row of the permission matrix (both the allowed and the refused case, for every Admin-only action), CSRF rejection, Post and Page create/read/update/delete, slug generation and stability, First-published date rules, Dashboard counts by role, Content list filtering, Preview matching public output, user management and Password reset, and Display name changes.\n- **Seam 2: the published site on disk.** Call the publish step against seeded data into a temporary folder and read the HTML files. Cover: Drafts and unpublished content absent; sanitized Markdown (raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms stripped); Navigation built from published Pages; Announcements ordering and the five-item Home page; byline uses the Display name and never the username; \"Updated\" date shown after later edits; only relative `href` and `src` values; approved image files copied; the Welcome text present.\n- **Seam 3 (small smoke test): the `cms` command.** First-Admin creation from an environment password, and a clean-setup run from `.env.example`. Kept small and separate.\n- **Prior art.** `tests/conftest.py` already provides the app and `client_as` fixtures, and the walking-skeleton test shows the style. Access-control tests should follow the one-line pattern in the `conftest.py` docstring.\n- **Test-first.** Each ticket starts with failing tests. Read the tests before letting them pass, to catch a test written against a misunderstanding.\n- **Security checks.** Drafts never appear in the export, no plain password in any response or log, no root-absolute paths in the export, sanitized output, CSRF on every state-changing form, and server-side enforcement of every Admin-only action.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- A separate Event content type, an event-date field, and automatic upcoming/past sorting.\n- Photo upload forms, automatic gallery management, and photo approvals enforced by software. (The Photos page with approved images is in scope.)\n- Account deletion, and a first-login password change flow.\n- Email sending, including email-based password reset.\n- A \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- RSVPs and sign-ups, comments, search, and tags or categories.\n- Multi-site support, drag-and-drop page building, and a rich-text WYSIWYG editor.\n- Any claim about ASA's real history, members, leaders, schedule or approval process.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Release checklist.** Written as part of the project. It covers running publish and deploy, the relative-path check, adding approved image files, confirming Photo permission before a real photo is added, and the limit that an Editor cannot add an image file alone. For the class demo the project author runs it from their own laptop. ASA has no known person responsible for this step, and none is assumed.\n- **Photo permission** is a working rule for this project, not a known ASA policy.\n- **ADRs.** No new ADR was needed from the grill. Add one later only if a decision is hard to reverse and surprising.\n- **Vocabulary.** Use the terms in `CONTEXT.md` (Post, Announcements, Event announcement, Page, Published, Live, Display name, Username, Deactivated account, Permission refusal, and so on). Do not use \"Upcoming Events\" for the Announcements Minimum 8 characters.\nCMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin\nCMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=change-me-editor\n# Set after you deploy, e.g. https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nCMS_BASE_PATH=\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n\n[project.scripts]\ncms = \"app.cli:main\"\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\n\n[build-system]\nrequires = [\"hatchling\"]\nbuild-backend = \"hatchling.build\"\n\n[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]\npackages = [\"app\"]\n M notes/usage-ledger.csv\n?? docs/transcripts/iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_10_your-name_20261001.md\n?? docs/transcripts/iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_11_your-name_20261001.md","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"0e0f8fa8-0374-482f-8796-9deb96dca310","timestamp":"2026-10-13T00:58:57.068Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"## Problem Statement\n\nASA, the African Student Association at Kenyon, is described in the client brief as a student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. Students need an easy way to find event announcements (including an Afrobeat event), learn about the association, explore cultural resources, and see photos from past activities. Its leaders need event announcements to be quick to publish, information about ASA to stay easy to find in the navigation, and a way to share photos only when ASA has permission to use them. One ASA leader should manage accounts and permanent pages; another member should be able to write and update event posts without a complicated form.\n\nThis is a class project (IPHS 400, Mini-Project #2). No claim is made about any real ASA process, officers, schedule or history. Terms below are defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS. A local admin console lets an Admin and Editors write **Posts** and **Pages**, manage accounts, and preview content. A `cms publish` step renders only **Published** content into a static public site, and `cms deploy` sends it to GitHub Pages, at which point the content is **Live**. The admin console never goes on the public internet (ADR-001).\n\nThe public site has a **Home page** (a short **Welcome text** taken from the client brief plus the five latest **Announcements**), an **Announcements** list, and **Navigation** built from published Pages (starter Pages for the demo: About ASA, Resources, Photos). Event announcements are ordinary Posts with the event's date, time, location and who can attend written in the **Body**. Photos are images inside Posts or Pages; there is no upload form.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Signing in\n1. As an Admin, I want to sign in with a username and password, so that only authorised people can change the site.\n2. As an Editor, I want to sign in and out, so that my session ends when I leave a shared computer.\n3. As an account owner, I want my password stored hashed, so that nobody, including the Admin, can read it.\n4. As an Admin, I want a wrong password to be rejected with a clear message that does not reveal whether the username exists, so that accounts cannot be guessed.\n5. As someone with a Deactivated account, I want sign-in to be refused, so that a former member can no longer change the site.\n6. As a signed-in user, I want every form I submit to be protected against forged requests, so that another website cannot act as me.\n7. As a visitor who is not signed in, I want any admin address to send me to sign-in, so that I never see admin content.\n\n### First Admin and setup\n8. As the project owner, I want the first Admin account created from the command line with a password taken from the environment, so that no password is committed to Git.\n9. As the project owner, I want a clean clone to run from `.env.example` plus a few documented steps, so that a grader can reproduce the demo.\n10. As the project owner, I want the database and `.env` kept out of Git, so that private data is never published.\n11. As the project owner, I want demo data that can be rebuilt on demand, so that screenshots and tests are repeatable.\n\n### Roles and permission refusal\n12. As an Admin, I want to manage accounts and permanent Pages, so that I control who can change the site and what the Navigation contains.\n13. As an Editor, I want to create and publish Posts directly, so that an announcement can go out quickly.\n14. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post, including another Editor's, so that event details can be corrected close to the event if the writer is unavailable.\n15. As an Editor, I want to update the Body of an existing Page, so that the Photos page can stay current.\n16. As an Admin, I want only Admins to delete Posts, so that a mistaken deletion is unlikely.\n17. As an Admin, I want only Admins to create, delete, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug a Page, so that Navigation and links stay stable.\n18. As an Admin, I want only Admins to change a slug, and to be warned that doing so can break an old link, so that shared links keep working.\n19. As an Editor, I want admin-only controls hidden from my screens, so that my screens stay simple.\n20. As an Editor who reaches an Admin-only address or submits a forbidden action directly, I want a clear \"You don't have permission\" page with a link back to the dashboard, so that I understand what happened.\n21. As an Admin, I want every permission enforced by the server, not by hidden buttons, so that access control is real.\n\n### Posts\n22. As an Editor, I want to write a Post with a title and a Body and save it as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it is ready for the public site.\n24. As an Editor, I want to unpublish a Post, so that a wrong announcement stops going out.\n25. As an Editor, I want the slug generated from my title on first save, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n26. As an Editor, I want a number added automatically when a slug already exists, so that two Posts never collide.\n27. As an Editor, I want the slug to stay unchanged when I correct the title or event details, so that shared links keep working.\n28. As an Editor, I want a short hint reminding me to include What, When, Where and Who can attend, so that announcements are complete.\n29. As an Editor, I want the hint not pre-filled into the Body and hideable without losing content, so that I can write naturally.\n30. As an Editor, I want the Post to record me as its Author automatically, so that I do not fill in extra fields.\n31. As an Editor, I want the Post's created, updated and first-published times recorded automatically, so that dates are trustworthy.\n\n### Pages\n32. As an Admin, I want to create a Page with a title, slug and Body, so that permanent information has a home.\n33. As an Admin, I want a published Page to appear in the public Navigation automatically, so that visitors can find it.\n34. As an Admin, I want an unpublished Page to disappear from the Navigation, so that unfinished pages are not linked.\n35. As an Admin, I want to delete a Page, so that obsolete pages can be removed.\n36. As an Editor, I want to edit the Body of a Page but see title, slug, status and delete controls as unavailable, so that I cannot break the Navigation.\n\n### Writing, preview and images\n37. As an Editor, I want to use headings, emphasis, lists, links and images with alt text, so that announcements read well without learning HTML.\n38. As an Editor, I want raw HTML, scripts, frames and forms in my text stripped, so that the site is safe.\n39. As an Editor, I want a preview that shows exactly what the public page will render, so that there are no surprises after publishing.\n40. As an Editor, I want to write a caption, alt text and Markdown reference for an image, so that photos are accessible.\n41. As an Editor, I understand I cannot add a new image file myself, so that the release-holder can confirm Photo permission first.\n42. As the release-holder, I want approved image files copied into the public site with relative paths, so that photos show up after deployment.\n43. As the release-holder, I want demo illustrations labelled as illustrative and never presented as photos of real ASA events, so that visitors are not misled.\n\n### Admin console\n44. As an Admin, I want a dashboard with the counts of Published Posts, Draft Posts, Published Pages and Draft Pages, so that I see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As an Admin, I want the dashboard to also show the number of active and Deactivated accounts, so that I can keep track of who has access.\n46. As an Editor, I want the dashboard to show the four content counts but no account counts, so that I only see what I need.\n47. As any signed-in user, I want a reminder on the dashboard that marking content Published does not make it Live until `cms publish` and `cms deploy` run, so that I do not expect instant changes.\n48. As any signed-in user, I want one Content list I can filter by Post or Page and by Draft or Published, so that I can find content without opening each item.\n49. As any signed-in user, I want each row to show title, status, Display name and last-updated time, so that I can tell items apart.\n50. As a phone user, I want the admin console usable at phone width, so that I can post from anywhere.\n\n### User management\n51. As an Admin, I want to create an account with a username, a private password, a role and a public Display name, so that a new member can start writing.\n52. As an Admin, I want to change an account's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n53. As an Admin, I want to deactivate an account, so that a former member can no longer sign in while their published Posts stay.\n54. As an Admin, I want to reactivate a deactivated account, so that a mistake is recoverable.\n55. As an Admin, I want to set a new password for an existing account without seeing the old one, so that a lost password can be recovered.\n56. As an Admin, I want a reset password never printed or logged, so that it cannot leak.\n57. As an Admin, I want to change an account's Display name, so that a former member can ask for their name to be replaced with \"ASA Events Team\".\n58. As an Admin, I want the original Author link of every Post kept, even after a Display name change or deactivation, so that the record stays accurate.\n59. As an Admin, I want the private username never used as a byline by default, so that private account names do not appear publicly.\n60. As an Admin, I want accounts deactivated rather than deleted, so that history is preserved.\n\n### Public site\n61. As a first-time visitor, I want a short welcome on the Home page, so that I know what ASA is and that I am welcome.\n62. As a visitor, I want the five latest Announcements on the Home page with a link to all of them, so that I can see what is new.\n63. As a visitor, I want an Announcements page listing all Published Posts, newest first by first-published date, so that I can browse.\n64. As a visitor, I want each Announcement as a clear Event card showing its title, first-published date and byline, so that I can scan quickly on a phone.\n65. As a visitor, I want an \"Updated\" date on a card when the content changed after first publishing, so that I know details were corrected.\n66. As a visitor, I want the event's actual date, time, location and who can attend in the Body, and the publication date never labelled as the event date, so that I am not misled.\n67. As a visitor, I want a Post to keep its original first-published date if it is unpublished and later published again, so that the order is stable.\n68. As a visitor, I want the Navigation to list Announcements and every published Page (About ASA, Resources, Photos for the demo), so that information is easy to find.\n69. As a visitor, I want the Photos page to say that actual event photos will be added when ASA has permission to use them, so that placeholders are not mistaken for real events.\n70. As a visitor, I want the public site to work on a phone with readable text, so that I can use it anywhere.\n71. As a visitor who uses a keyboard or screen reader, I want a sensible heading order, readable contrast, visible focus, keyboard access to all controls, and alt text on every image, so that the site is accessible.\n72. As a visitor, I want Drafts and unpublished content never to appear anywhere in the public site, so that unfinished work stays private.\n73. As a visitor, I want the site to work from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no link or style is broken.\n\n### Releasing\n74. As the release-holder, I want `cms publish` to write the public site from Published content only, so that Drafts never leave the database.\n75. As the release-holder, I want `cms deploy` to send the result to GitHub Pages, so that content becomes Live.\n76. As the release-holder, I want a short release checklist covering publish, deploy, checking relative paths, adding approved images, and confirming Photo permission, so that the step is quick and repeatable.\n77. As the release-holder, I want the checklist to state that an Editor cannot add an image file alone, so that clients are not surprised.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture is fixed** by ADR-001 (local admin console, static public site) and ADR-002 (FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, argon2, Markdown sanitizer). No new dependencies.\n- **Content model.** Two kinds of content only: Post and Page. No separate Event type and no event-date field. A Post has a title, slug, Markdown Body, status (Draft or Published), Author, and created, updated and first-published times. A Page has the same fields except that the Author is optional for display and a Page does not appear in the Announcements list.\n- **First-published date** is set the first time a Post becomes Published and never cleared, including when the Post is unpublished and republished. The **Updated date** on the public card is shown when the Body or title changes after the first-published date.\n- **Ordering.** Announcements are ordered by first-published date, newest first. Editing does not reorder. The Home page shows the five most recent; the Announcements page shows all Published Posts.\n- **Slugs.** A Post's slug is generated from its title on first save, made unique by adding a number, and never changed automatically. A Page's slug is entered by the Admin. Only the Admin can change any slug, and the form warns that this can break existing links. Slug edits are not shown to Editors.\n- **Accounts.** An account has a private username, a password hash, a role (Admin or Editor), a public Display name, and an active flag. There is no account deletion. Posts keep their Author link permanently. A Post's public byline is the Author's current Display name. The username is never used as a byline.\n- **Authentication.** Session cookie signed by the server. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and are never stored, shown or logged in plain form. Sign-in failures use one generic message. A Deactivated account cannot sign in and any existing session for it stops working.\n- **Authorization.** A single central rule table maps each action to the roles allowed. Every state-changing route checks it on the server. Templates hide controls the current role cannot use, but hiding is never the protection. A refused action shows a \"You don't have permission\" page with a link to the dashboard, and a not-signed-in visitor is sent to sign-in.\n- **Permission matrix.** Admin: everything. Editor: sign in and out; create, edit and publish or unpublish Posts, including other people's; edit the Body of an existing Page; view dashboard counts and the Content list. Editor cannot: delete Posts or Pages; create, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug Pages; change any slug; open user management or change any account, role or Display name; reset passwords.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies.\n- **Markdown and sanitizing.** Allowed: headings, emphasis, lists, links and images with alt text. Raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms are stripped. The same rendering and sanitizing path is used for the admin preview and the public export, so the preview matches the public page.\n- **Images.** No upload feature. Approved image files are added to the project by the release-holder and copied into the public site by `cms publish`. Markdown references use relative paths. Demo illustrations are clearly labelled illustrative.\n- **Admin console screens.** Sign-in, Dashboard, Content list, Post editor with Preview and the Event details hint, Page editor (reduced controls for Editors), User management (Admin only), and the permission-refusal page. Layouts work at phone width.\n- **Dashboard.** Four content counts for everyone; active and deactivated account counts for the Admin only; a reminder that Published is not Live. No \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- **Content list.** One list of Posts and Pages, filterable by type and by status, with title, status, Display name and last-updated time on each row.\n- **Event details hint.** A short, dismissible hint near the Post editor listing What, When, Where and Who can attend. It is never inserted into the Body.\n- **Publishing.** `cms publish` renders Home, Announcements, each Published Post, each Published Page and the Navigation to plain HTML, using only Published content and only relative paths. It copies approved image files. `cms deploy` pushes the result to the `gh-pages` branch. Nothing is Live until both have run.\n- **Public design.** Polished, mobile-first, readable text, clear Event cards, a few appropriately licensed images or decorative graphics that are never presented as real ASA event photos. Accessibility requirements: sensible heading order, readable contrast, visible focus and full keyboard access, phone-width layout, and alt text on every image.\n- **Content carried from the client brief.** The Welcome text uses only the brief's wording. Starter Pages (About ASA, Resources, Photos) and seed Posts are demo placeholders and contain no claims about ASA's real history, officers, members, schedule or approval process.\n- **First Admin.** Created from the command line at setup, with the password read from the environment. No password, `.env` or database file is committed. A clean clone runs from `.env.example` plus documented steps.\n- **Demo data.** The seed data is rebuilt on demand and includes both roles, published and draft Posts and Pages, and a deactivated account.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **A good test checks external behaviour only:** what a signed-in user sees and can do, and what files the publish step writes. It does not check internal functions, the database layout or template details.\n- **Seam 1: the admin console over HTTP.** Use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. Cover sign-in and sign-out, Deactivated accounts, each row of the permission matrix (both the allowed and the refused case, for every Admin-only action), CSRF rejection, Post and Page create/read/update/delete, slug generation and stability, First-published date rules, Dashboard counts by role, Content list filtering, Preview matching public output, user management and Password reset, and Display name changes.\n- **Seam 2: the published site on disk.** Call the publish step against seeded data into a temporary folder and read the HTML files. Cover: Drafts and unpublished content absent; sanitized Markdown (raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms stripped); Navigation built from published Pages; Announcements ordering and the five-item Home page; byline uses the Display name and never the username; \"Updated\" date shown after later edits; only relative `href` and `src` values; approved image files copied; the Welcome text present.\n- **Seam 3 (small smoke test): the `cms` command.** First-Admin creation from an environment password, and a clean-setup run from `.env.example`. Kept small and separate.\n- **Prior art.** `tests/conftest.py` already provides the app and `client_as` fixtures, and the walking-skeleton test shows the style. Access-control tests should follow the one-line pattern in the `conftest.py` docstring.\n- **Test-first.** Each ticket starts with failing tests. Read the tests before letting them pass, to catch a test written against a misunderstanding.\n- **Security checks.** Drafts never appear in the export, no plain password in any response or log, no root-absolute paths in the export, sanitized output, CSRF on every state-changing form, and server-side enforcement of every Admin-only action.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- A separate Event content type, an event-date field, and automatic upcoming/past sorting.\n- Photo upload forms, automatic gallery management, and photo approvals enforced by software. (The Photos page with approved images is in scope.)\n- Account deletion, and a first-login password change flow.\n- Email sending, including email-based password reset.\n- A \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- RSVPs and sign-ups, comments, search, and tags or categories.\n- Multi-site support, drag-and-drop page building, and a rich-text WYSIWYG editor.\n- Any claim about ASA's real history, members, leaders, schedule or approval process.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Release checklist.** Written as part of the project. It covers running publish and deploy, the relative-path check, adding approved image files, confirming Photo permission before a real photo is added, and the limit that an Editor cannot add an image file alone. For the class demo the project author runs it from their own laptop. ASA has no known person responsible for this step, and none is assumed.\n- **Photo permission** is a working rule for this project, not a known ASA policy.\n- **ADRs.** No new ADR was needed from the grill. Add one later only if a decision is hard to reverse and surprising.\n- **Vocabulary.** Use the terms in `CONTEXT.md` (Post, Announcements, Event announcement, Page, Published, Live, Display name, Username, Deactivated account, Permission refusal, and so on). Do not use \"Upcoming Events\" for the Announcements
