The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Spec review of #12: the diff mostly meets the criteria, with three real gaps and one vacuous assertion.**\n\nI ran the 20 new tests (all pass) and ran `scripts/check_backends.py` against the repo (exit 0). I also probed the check with throwaway inputs. The tags are unmoved (`e3b0788…`, `06a3070…`), `pyproject.toml` is untouched, and nothing contacts GitHub.\n\n**(a) Missing or partly met**\n- **Draft after a second deploy.** The criterion reads \"A Draft Post, and a Post that was Published and then unpublished, are not on `gh-pages` after a second deploy.\" `test_no_draft_reaches_the_pages_branch` deploys once only. The second-deploy test has no Draft. A Draft that appears only on redeploy would not be noticed.\n- **Vacuous slug assertion.** In the same test, `\"quiet-draft\" not in pages_files(...)` compares against a set of full paths such as `posts/quiet-draft.html`, so it can never fail. Only the \"Quiet Draft\" title grep does any work. A leaked draft with a changed title or an unlinked page would pass.\n- **Trailer discovery.** The criterion says the check reads \"every `Backend:` commit trailer in the history\". `TRAILER` is case-sensitive and anchored at column 0. I confirmed that these all return no findings:\n  - `backend: openrouter x`\n  - `&gt; Backend: openrouter x`\n  - `    Backend: openrouter x`\n- **Trailer model not compared.** `Backend: anthropic Opus 9` returns no findings, because trailer models are never compared to the table.\n\n**(c) Looks right, but a regression would slip through**\n- **Table in a code block.** A table inside a fenced block is parsed as the real one. Nothing is checked about fences.\n- **Model spelling.** The ledger model `sonnet 5.5` matches `Sonnet 5.5` case-insensitively, but `Sonnet-5.5` is flagged. Spelling is held to an exact match apart from case, and that is fine. Whether the case-folding is intended is worth confirming.\n- **Empty history or ledger.** An empty history passes. That is acceptable for the \"no trailers\" state, but `git log` returning nothing is indistinguishable from \"no trailers\". `check=True` does at least make a git failure loud.\n- **Two Anthropic rows.** A second Anthropic row passes silently. The ledger-model check unions all rows for a provider.\n- **Co-Authored-By lines.** They are not mistaken for trailers.\n- **ChatGPT disclosure.** The check is a bare substring match anywhere in the README, including prose and code comments.\n- **Deploy tests.**\n  - The `main`-not-pushed and exact-tree assertions are good, and the byte-for-byte check works.\n  - The tests call `render_site` themselves and then `main([\"deploy\"])`. They do not exercise the real `cms publish` to `cms deploy` path. They also run from a `work` cwd while `site/` lives elsewhere, so \"wrong working directory\" is not tested.\n  - The https-remote test only asserts `!= 0`. It does not check that the failure comes from the push, rather than from some other cause.\n  - Nothing checks that the other branches of the remote are left alone.\n\n**(b) Scope creep (mild)**\n- `check_backends.py` adds rules the issue did not ask for:\n  - A trailer provider must also be in the ledger.\n  - A non-Anthropic row must not say \"none\" in its trailer column.\n  - The model-per-provider check.\n- The `trailers()` helper is used only by one test.\n- `test_chatgpt_disclosure_sits_outside_the_table` tests README layout rather than the check.\n\nNo invented usage rows, comments or timestamps appear in the in-scope files. The one-line README change is fine. I ignored `notes/usage-ledger.csv` and `docs/mp2-self-assessment.md`, as instructed.\n\n**Files**\n- `/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t10_deploy.py`\n- `/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/scripts/check_backends.py`\n- `/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t10_backends.py`</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>35795</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>5</tool_uses><duration_ms>38898</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

\"\"\"A working repository whose `origin` is a local bare repository (`.bare`), site at `.work/site`.\"\"\"\n    for name in GIT_REDIRECTS:\n        monkeypatch.delenv(name, raising=False)\n    for name, value in GIT_ISOLATION.items():\n        monkeypatch.setenv(name, value)\n    bare, work = tmp_path / \"pages-remote.git\", tmp_path / \"work\"\n    git(\"init\", \"--bare\", \"-q\", git(\"add\", \".\", cwd=work)\n    git(\"commit\", \"-qm\", \"initial\", cwd=work)\n    monkeypatch.chdir(work)\n    # The only place anything can be pushed is a folder on this machine.\n    assert git(\"add\", \".\", cwd=work)\n    git(\"commit\", \"-qm\", \"initial\", cwd=work)\n    monkeypatch.chdir(work)\n    # The only place anything can be pushed is a folder on this machine.\n    assert test\"])\n    return code, capsys.readouterr().out\n\n\ndef test_deploy_pushes_every_exported_file_to_gh_pages_and_nothing_else(remote, capsys):\n    add_post(remote.db, \"Afrobeat Night\", \"What: main([\"deploy\"]) != 0","+","+    assert \"transport 'https' not allowed\" in capfd.readouterr().err"]}],"originalFile":"\"\"\"T10: `cms deploy` pushes the export to the Pages branch, tested without GitHub.\n\nSeam 3 (the `cms` command). The \"remote\" is a bare Git repository in a temporary\nfolder, and Git is limited to the `file` protocol, so nothing here can reach the\nnetwork. This exercises the same `ghp_import` call the real deploy makes.\n\"\"\"\nimport os\nimport subprocess\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import posts, settings\nfrom app.cli import main\nfrom app.publish import render_site\nfrom tests.test_t03_publish import add_post\n\n\ndef git(*args, cwd=None, git_dir=None, binary=False):\n    command = [\"git\"] + ([\"--git-dir\", str(git_dir)] if git_dir else []) + list(args)\n    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, check=True, text=not binary)\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef pages_remote(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"A working repository whose `origin` is a local bare repository. Returns that bare repo.\"\"\"\n    for name, value in {\"GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL\": \"file\", \"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL\": os.devnull,\n                        \"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM\": os.devnull, \"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT\": \"0\",\n                        \"GIT_AUTHOR_NAME\": \"Test\", \"GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL\": \"test@example.com\",\n                        \"GIT_COMMITTER_NAME\": \"Test\", \"GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL\": \"test@example.com\"}.items():\n        monkeypatch.setenv(name, value)\n    bare = tmp_path / \"pages-remote.git\"\n    git(\"init\", \"--bare\", \"-q\", str(bare))\n    work = tmp_path / \"work\"\n    work.mkdir()\n    git(\"init\", \"-q\", cwd=work)\n    git(\"remote\", \"add\", \"origin\", str(bare), cwd=work)\n    (work / \"README\").write_text(\"the project, not the site\")\n    git(\"add\", \".\", cwd=work)\n    git(\"commit\", \"-qm\", \"initial\", cwd=work)\n    monkeypatch.chdir(work)\n    # Nothing can be pushed anywhere except a folder on this machine.\n    assert git(\"remote\", \"get-url\", \"origin\", cwd=work).strip() == str(bare)\n    return bare\n\n\ndef pages_files(bare):\n    return set(git(\"ls-tree\", \"-r\", \"--name-only\", \"gh-pages\", git_dir=bare).split())\n\n\ndef deploy(db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    site = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\", database=db_path)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SITE\", site)\n    code = main([\"deploy\", \"--message\", \"Publish test\"])\n    return site, code, capsys.readouterr().out\n\n\ndef test_deploy_pushes_every_exported_file_to_gh_pages_and_nothing_else(\n        db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys, pages_remote):\n    add_post(db_path, \"Afrobeat Night\", \"What: music\")\n    add_post(db_path, \"Quiet Draft\", \"not for the public\", published=False)\n\n    site, code, out = deploy(db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys)\n\n    assert code == 0 and \"Pushed to gh-pages\" in out\n    exported = {str(p.relative_to(site)) for p in site.rglob(\"*\") if p.is_file()}\n    assert exported <= pages_files(pages_remote)              # .nojekyll is the only extra\n    assert pages_files(pages_remote) - exported == {\".nojekyll\"}\n    for name in exported:                                      # byte for byte\n        assert git(\"show\", f\"gh-pages:{name}\", git_dir=pages_remote, binary=True) == \\\n            (site / name).read_bytes(), name\n    assert \"posts/afrobeat-night.html\" in pages_files(pages_remote)\n    assert git(\"branch\", \"--list\", git_dir=pages_remote).split() == [\"gh-pages\"]   # no main pushed\n\n\ndef test_no_draft_reaches_the_pages_branch(db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys, pages_remote):\n    add_post(db_path, \"Afrobeat Night\", \"What: music\")\n    add_post(db_path, \"Quiet Draft\", \"not for the public\", published=False)\n    deploy(db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys)\n    everything = \"\".join(\n        git(\"show\", f\"gh-pages:{name}\", git_dir=pages_remote)\n        for name in pages_files(pages_remote) if name.endswith((\".html\", \".css\")))\n    assert \"Quiet Draft\" not in everything and \"quiet-draft\" not in pages_files(pages_remote)\n\n\ndef test_a_second_deploy_replaces_the_branch_so_an_unpublished_post_is_gone(\n        db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys, pages_remote):\n    post_id = add_post(db_path, \"Afrobeat Night\", \"What: music\")\n    add_post(db_path, \"Movie Evening\", \"What: film\")\n    deploy(db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys)\n    assert {\"posts/afrobeat-night.html\", \"posts/movie-evening.html\"} <= pages_files(pages_remote)\n\n    posts.unpublish(db_path, post_id)\n    _, code, _ = deploy(db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    files = pages_files(pages_remote)\n    assert \"posts/afrobeat-night.html\" not in files and \"posts/movie-evening.html\" in files\n    announcements = git(\"show\", \"gh-pages:announcements.html\", git_dir=pages_remote)\n    assert \"Afrobeat Night\" not in announcements and \"Movie Evening\" in announcements\n    assert len(git(\"rev-list\", \"gh-pages\", git_dir=pages_remote).split()) == 2    # a new commit\n\n\ndef test_deploy_refuses_when_there_is_no_site_and_pushes_nothing(\n        tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys, pages_remote):\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SITE\", tmp_path / \"no-such-site\")\n    assert main([\"deploy\"]) == 1\n    assert \"cms publish\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n    assert git(\"branch\", \"--list\", git_dir=pages_remote).strip() == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_deploy_cannot_reach_a_network_remote_in_this_test(\n        db_path, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys, pages_remote):\n    \"\"\"The safety net the other tests rely on: with only `file` allowed, an https remote fails.\"\"\"\n    work = tmp_path / \"work\"\n    git(\"remote\", \"set-url\", \"origin\", \"https://github.com/example/never-contacted.git\", cwd=work)\n    site = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\", database=db_path)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SITE\", site)\n    assert main([\"deploy\"]) != 0\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b6b17882-c184-43e6-90e1-d795f2696f64","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a77ef331-d963-4153-904a-5fde226c3f3f","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

the README's Backends used table agrees with the ledger and the commit trailers.\n\nThe three places that must agree (the rubric's H6): the table, the ledger's\n`provider` and `model` columns, and `Backend: <provider> <model>` commit trailers.\nChatGPT is separate planning assistance outside Claude Code, so it is disclosed in\nthe README's own words but is never a table row, a ledger provider or a trailer.\n`scripts/check_backends.py` does the checking; these tests run it on the real\nrepository and on deliberately broken copies, so the check cannot pass by accident.\n\"\"\"\nimport importlib.util\nimport re\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nspec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(\"check_backends\", ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"check_backends.py\")\ncheck_backends = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\nspec.loader.exec_module(check_backends)\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef readme():\n    return (ROOT / \"README.md\").read_text()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef ledger():\n    return check_backends.read_ledger()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef history():\n    return check_backends.read_history()\n\n\ndef problems(readme, ledger, history):\n    return check_backends.check(readme, ledger, history)\n\n\ndef with_extra_table_row(readme, row):\n    \"\"\"The README with one more row directly under the Backends table's separator line.\"\"\"\n    heading = readme.index(\"### Backends used\")\n    separator = readme.index(\"|---\", heading)\n    end = readme.index(\"\\n\", separator)\n    return readme[:end + 1] + row + \"\\n\" + readme[end + 1:]\n\n\nBACKUP_ROW = \"| OpenRouter | some-model | the backup | `Backend: openrouter some-model` |\"\n\n\n# -- the real repository -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_the_real_readme_ledger_and_history_agree(readme, ledger, history):\n    assert problems(readme, ledger, history) == []\n\n\ndef test_the_real_check_reads_what_it_should(readme, ledger, history):\n    table = check_backends.parse_table(readme)\n    assert [row[\"provider\"].lower() for row in table] == [\"anthropic\"]\n    assert {r[\"provider\"].lower() for r in ledger} == {\"anthropic\"}\n    assert check_backends.trailer_pairs(history) == []\n\n\ndef test_the_command_passes_on_this_repository():\n    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"check_backends.py\")],\n                            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert result.returncode == 0 and \"agree\" in result.stdout\n\n\n# -- every kind of disagreement is caught, each by its own message -----------------------------\n\ndef test_a_ledger_provider_missing_from_the_table_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"some-model\"}]\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"Ledger provider 'openrouter' has no row in the Backends table\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_ledger_backup_with_no_commit_trailer_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"some-model\"}]\n    found = problems(with_extra_table_row(readme, BACKUP_ROW), ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"in the ledger but no commit has a 'Backend: openrouter\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_commit_trailer_for_a_provider_not_in_the_table_or_the_ledger_is_caught_twice_over(\n        readme, ledger, history):\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history + \"\\nBackend: openrouter some-model\\n\")\n    assert any(\"trailer names 'openrouter'\" in p and \"no row in the Backends table\" in p for p in found)\n    assert any(\"trailer names 'openrouter'\" in p and \"ledger's provider column never records\" in p\n               for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_table_row_nobody_used_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    found = problems(with_extra_table_row(readme, BACKUP_ROW), ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"lists 'openrouter', but neither the ledger nor any commit trailer shows it used\" in p\n               for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_ledger_model_missing_from_the_table_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"anthropic\", \"model\": \"Haiku 5.5\"}]\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"Ledger model 'Haiku 5.5'\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_trailer_model_the_table_does_not_list_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history + \"\\nBackend: anthropic Opus 9\\n\")\n    assert any(\"'Backend: anthropic Opus 9' names a model that is not in the table\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_backup_row_whose_trailer_column_says_none_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(readme, \"| OpenRouter | some-model | the backup | none needed |\")\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"some-model\"}]\n    history = history + \"\\nBackend: openrouter some-model\\n\"\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"trailer column for 'openrouter' says none\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_complete_backup_declaration_passes(readme, ledger, history):\n    \"\"\"The positive control: table row, ledger rows and a trailer, all agreeing, give no problem.\"\"\"\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(readme, BACKUP_ROW)\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"some-model\"}]\n    assert problems(readme, ledger, history + \"\\nBackend: openrouter some-model\\n\") == []\n\n\n# -- trailers are found however git or a person writes them -----------------------------------------\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", [\"backend: openrouter some-model\", \"BACKEND: openrouter some-model\",\n                                  \"    Backend: openrouter some-model\", \"Backend:openrouter   some-model  \"])\ndef test_a_trailer_is_found_in_any_case_and_spacing(line):\n    assert check_backends.trailer_pairs(f\"Subject\\n\\nBody\\n\\n{line}\\n\") == [(\"openrouter\", \"some-model\")]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", [\"Backend: <provider> <model>\", \"> Backend: openrouter some-model\",\n                                  \"Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\",\n                                  \"The Backend: line is explained in the README\"])\ndef test_a_placeholder_a_quotation_or_another_trailer_is_not_a_trailer(line):\n    assert check_backends.trailer_pairs(f\"Subject\\n\\n{line}\\n\") == []\n\n\ndef test_a_model_id_containing_a_slash_is_one_model(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(readme, \"| OpenRouter | vendor/model-x | the backup | `Backend:` trailer |\")\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"vendor/model-x\"}]\n    assert problems(readme, ledger, history + \"\\nBackend: openrouter vendor/model-x\\n\") == []\n\n\n# -- ChatGPT is separate planning assistance ---------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_chatgpt_as_a_backends_row_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(readme, \"| OpenAI | ChatGPT | planning | none needed |\")\n    assert any(\"ChatGPT is listed in the Backends table\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_chatgpt_as_a_ledger_provider_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"chatgpt\", \"model\": \"ChatGPT\"}]\n    assert any(\"ChatGPT appears in the ledger\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_chatgpt_as_a_commit_trailer_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    history = history + \"\\nBackend: openai ChatGPT\\n\"\n    assert any(\"trailer names ChatGPT\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_a_note_that_is_not_chatgpt_in_the_used_for_column_is_not_a_backend_row(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = readme.replace(\"| none needed |\", \"| none needed (ChatGPT was not used here) |\")\n    assert not any(\"listed in the Backends table\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_chatgpt_help_that_is_not_disclosed_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    undisclosed = readme.replace(\"ChatGPT\", \"an assistant\")\n    assert any(\"not disclosed\" in p for p in problems(undisclosed, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_a_mention_of_chatgpt_only_inside_a_code_block_is_not_a_disclosure(readme, ledger, history):\n    hidden = readme.replace(\"ChatGPT\", \"an assistant\") + \"\\n```\\nChatGPT\\n```\\n\"\n    assert any(\"not disclosed\" in p for p in problems(hidden, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_the_real_readme_discloses_chatgpt_in_prose_and_keeps_it_out_of_the_table(readme):\n    assert \"chatgpt\" in check_backends.prose(readme).lower()\n    assert all(\"chatgpt\" not in \" \".join(row.values()).lower() for row in check_backends.parse_table(readme))\n\n\n# -- the table must be readable, and the history must be readable -------------------------------\n\ndef test_a_readme_with_no_backends_table_is_caught(ledger, history):\n    found = problems(\"# Project\\n\\nNothing here.\\n\", ledger, history)\n    assert len(found) == 1 and \"no readable 'Backends used' table\" in found[0]\n\n\ndef test_a_table_inside_a_code_block_is_not_the_real_table(readme, ledger, history):\n    start = readme.index(\"### Backends used\")\n    table = re.search(r\"(\\|.*\\n)+\", readme[start:]).group(0)\n    fenced = readme.replace(table, \"```\\n\" + table + \"```\\n\")\n    found = problems(fenced, ledger, history)\n    assert len(found) == 1 and \"no readable 'Backends used' table\" in found[0]\n\n\ndef test_an_unreadable_or_empty_history_is_an_error_not_a_pass(monkeypatch, capsys):\n    def fail():\n        raise RuntimeError(\"git log returned no commits, so the trailers cannot be checked.\")\n    monkeypatch.setattr(check_backends, \"read_history\", fail)\n    assert check_backends.main() == 1\n    assert \"Cannot check the backends\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n\n\ndef test_read_history_refuses_an_empty_log(monkeypatch):\n    class Done:\n        stdout = \"\\n\"\n    monkeypatch.setattr(check_backends.subprocess, \"run\", lambda *a, **k: Done())\n    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match=\"no commits\"):\n        check_backends.read_history()\n\n\ndef test_read_history_reports_a_git_failure_plainly(monkeypatch):\n    def broken(*args, **kwargs):\n        raise subprocess.CalledProcessError(128, \"git\")\n    monkeypatch.setattr(check_backends.subprocess, \"run\", broken)\n    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match=\"Could not read the commit history\"):\n check_backends.read_history()"]}],"originalFile":"\"\"\"T10: the README's Backends used table agrees with the ledger and the commit trailers.\n\nThe three places that must agree (the rubric's H6): the table, the ledger's\n`provider` and `model` columns, and `Backend: <provider> <model>` commit trailers.\nChatGPT is separate planning assistance outside Claude Code, so it is disclosed in\nthe README but is never a table row, a ledger provider or a trailer.\n`scripts/check_backends.py` does the checking; these tests run it on the real\nrepository and on deliberately broken copies, so the check cannot pass by accident.\n\"\"\"\nimport csv\nimport importlib.util\nimport io\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nspec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(\"check_backends\", ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"check_backends.py\")\ncheck_backends = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\nspec.loader.exec_module(check_backends)\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef readme():\n    return (ROOT / \"README.md\").read_text()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef ledger():\n    with (ROOT / \"notes\" / \"usage-ledger.csv\").open() as handle:\n        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef history():\n    return subprocess.run([\"git\", \"log\", \"--all\", \"--format=%B\"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True,\n                          text=True, check=True).stdout\n\n\ndef problems(readme, ledger, history):\n    return check_backends.check(readme, ledger, history)\n\n\ndef with_extra_table_row(readme, row):\n    marker = \"| Anthropic | Sonnet 5 / Sonnet 5.5 |\"\n    start = readme.index(marker)\n    end = readme.index(\"\\n\", start)\n    return readme[:end + 1] + row + \"\\n\" + readme[end + 1:]\n\n\n# -- the real repository -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_the_real_readme_ledger_and_history_agree(readme, ledger, history):\n    assert problems(readme, ledger, history) == []\n\n\ndef test_the_real_check_reads_what_it_should(readme, ledger, history):\n    table = check_backends.parse_table(readme)\n    assert [row[\"provider\"].lower() for row in table] == [\"anthropic\"]\n    assert {r[\"provider\"].lower() for r in ledger} == {\"anthropic\"}\n    assert check_backends.trailers(history) == set()\n\n\ndef test_the_command_passes_on_this_repository():\n    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"check_backends.py\")],\n                            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert result.returncode == 0 and \"agree\" in result.stdout\n\n\n# -- every kind of disagreement is caught ----------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_a_ledger_provider_missing_from_the_table_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"some-model\"}]\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"openrouter\" in p and \"table\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_ledger_backup_with_no_commit_trailer_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(\n        readme, \"| OpenRouter | some-model | the backup | `Backend: openrouter some-model` |\")\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"some-model\"}]\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"trailer\" in p and \"openrouter\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_commit_trailer_for_a_provider_not_in_the_table_or_the_ledger_is_caught_twice_over(\n        readme, ledger, history):\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history + \"\\nBackend: openrouter some-model\\n\")\n    # two separate disagreements, each named: no table row, and the ledger never records it\n    assert any(\"trailer names 'openrouter'\" in p and \"no row in the Backends table\" in p for p in found)\n    assert any(\"trailer names 'openrouter'\" in p and \"ledger's provider column never records\" in p\n               for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_table_row_nobody_used_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(\n        readme, \"| OpenRouter | some-model | the backup | `Backend: openrouter some-model` |\")\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"openrouter\" in p and (\"ledger\" in p or \"used\" in p) for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_ledger_model_missing_from_the_table_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"anthropic\", \"model\": \"Haiku 5.5\"}]\n    found = problems(readme, ledger, history)\n    assert any(\"Haiku 5.5\" in p for p in found)\n\n\ndef test_a_backup_row_whose_trailer_column_says_none_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(readme, \"| OpenRouter | some-model | the backup | none needed |\")\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"openrouter\", \"model\": \"some-model\"}]\n    history = history + \"\\nBackend: openrouter some-model\\n\"\n    assert any(\"none\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\n# -- ChatGPT is separate planning assistance ---------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_chatgpt_as_a_backends_row_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    readme = with_extra_table_row(readme, \"| OpenAI | ChatGPT | planning | none needed |\")\n    assert any(\"ChatGPT\" in p and \"table\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_chatgpt_as_a_ledger_provider_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    ledger = ledger + [{\"provider\": \"chatgpt\", \"model\": \"ChatGPT\"}]\n    assert any(\"ChatGPT\" in p and \"ledger\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_chatgpt_as_a_commit_trailer_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    history = history + \"\\nBackend: openai ChatGPT\\n\"\n    assert any(\"trailer names ChatGPT\" in p for p in problems(readme, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_chatgpt_help_that_is_not_disclosed_is_caught(readme, ledger, history):\n    undisclosed = readme.replace(\"ChatGPT\", \"an assistant\")\n    assert any(\"not disclosed\" in p for p in problems(undisclosed, ledger, history))\n\n\ndef test_chatgpt_disclosure_sits_outside_the_table(readme):\n    table_text = readme[readme.index(\"### Backends used\"):]\n    first_blank = table_text.index(\"\\n\\n\", table_text.index(\"|---\"))\n    assert \"ChatGPT\" not in table_text[:first_blank]          # the rows themselves\n    assert \"ChatGPT\" in readme[:readme.index(\"### Backends used\")]\n\n\n# -- the table must be readable at all ----------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_a_readme_with_no_backends_table_is_caught(ledger, history):\n    found = problems(\"# Project\\n\\nNothing here.\\n\", ledger, history)\n    assert len(found) == 1 and \"no readable 'Backends used' table\" in found[0]\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b1d624ab-b6b1-4fbf-9622-24cd2e02f1a9","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a77ef331-d963-4153-904a-5fde226c3f3f","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

I am calling it an equivalent-in-tests gap, not a pass.\n- **My first mutation run of the Backends check was invalid** (the file was untracked, so my restore step did nothing and mutations piled up). I discarded it, restored the file, and redid it with a copy-based restore. The honest run exposed four loose assertions, which I tightened before this commit. Both reviewers also found real problems (a dead filename assertion, a network test that could pass for the wrong reason, missing Git isolation variables, trailers in other cases or indented, a table hidden in a code block, model ids containing `/`, and an empty history passing), all fixed.\n\n## The score\n\"\"\")\n# E2 row and recheck section\na=s.index(\"| E2 | 2 |\"); b=s.index(\"\\n\",a)\ns=s[:a]+\"| E2 | 2 | 1 (conditional) | T03's criterion 7 (`cms deploy`) and T08's Backends table are now covered by behaviour tests. {"parentUuid":"c1168918-b4f6-48d5-b676-c17116a21c9c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfyX51Tj1mXSfgom6Yck6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01NhS7w1M7PuA91RPFuVpnYz","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yawoppong-krampah-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/a77ef331-d963-4153-904a-5fde226c3f3f/scratchpad/review12.md <<'EOF'\n## T10 `/code-review` (#12): findings and how each was resolved\n\nWorking tree against `HEAD` (`fa94a01`), 447 tests passing. Two independent reviewers (Standards, Spec). No hard violation of CLAUDE.md: no dependency added, no network, no secret.\n\n### Spec\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| A Draft was only checked on a first deploy; the criterion says after a second deploy | **Fixed**: the Draft stays in the database through two publish-and-deploy runs and is absent after each |\n| `\"quiet-draft\" not in <set of full paths>` can never fail | **Fixed**: `not any(\"quiet-draft\" in name for name in files)` |\n| Trailers were only found as `Backend:` at column 0, case-sensitive | **Fixed**: any case, indented; a placeholder `Backend: <provider> <model>`, a `> ` quotation and `Co-Authored-By:` are not trailers (parametrized tests) |\n| A trailer's model was never compared with the table | **Fixed**: `Backend: anthropic Opus 9` is reported |\n| A table inside a code block counted as the real table | **Fixed**: fenced blocks are removed before parsing; a test moves the real table into a fence |\n| ChatGPT \"disclosed\" by a bare substring anywhere (code blocks, table cells) | **Fixed**: it must appear in the README's prose; a mention only inside a fence is not a disclosure; only the provider and model cells are checked for it as a backend |\n| Deploy tests called `render_site` themselves and ran from a different directory than `site/` | **Fixed**: they now run the real `cms publish` then `cms deploy`, with the site at `<repo>/site` |\n| Other branches of the remote were not checked | **Fixed**: a test pushes `main` first and checks it is unchanged |\n| The https-remote test only asserted a non-zero exit | **Fixed**: it asserts git's own `transport 'https' not allowed` |\n| Empty or unreadable `git log` passed as \"no trailers\" | **Fixed**: `read_history()` raises, `main()` reports it and exits 1 (3 tests) |\n| Two Anthropic rows pass silently; case-insensitive model matching | Left: both are intended and harmless |\n| Extra rules not asked for (model per provider, \"none\" in a backup row, trailer provider in the ledger) | Accepted: they are what \"agree\" means for H6 |\n\n### Standards\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Fixture lacked `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and similar; under a Git hook they would point at the developer's repository | **Fixed**: all of them are removed from the environment for these tests |\n| Network test rebuilt a path the fixture owns | **Fixed**: the fixture returns the working repo, the bare repo, the site and the database together |\n| Redundant assertion; duplicated `git log` and CSV reading; `trailers()` used by one test | **Fixed**: removed, shared `read_ledger()` and `read_history()`, helper deleted |\n| A model id with a slash (`vendor/model`) was split in two | **Fixed**: only ` / ` and `;` or `,` separate models |\n| `with_extra_table_row` hard-coded a README row | **Fixed**: it inserts under the table's own separator line |\n| Messages tied to wording in some tests | Reduced: each negative control now asserts its own specific message |\n\n### How I checked the checks\n- A mutation run over `scripts/check_backends.py` and `cms deploy`: **28 of 29 breakages are caught**, each by a named test.\n- **The one not caught:** adding `-f` to the push of the same `gh-pages` branch. It behaves identically unless someone else pushed to `gh-pages` in between, which no test sets up. It is an equivalent-in-tests gap, not a pass.\n- **My first mutation run was invalid.** The script was untracked, so my `git checkout` restore did nothing and the mutations accumulated, making everything look caught. I restored the file, redid the run with a copy-based restore, found four loose assertions (a generic word like \"table\" let another message satisfy a test), and tightened them. Both files were compared byte for byte with their originals afterwards.\n\n### Not in this commit\n- The report paragraph for section 3 is drafted and held for your review.\n- Neither tag moved. No usage rows, comments, timestamps or extension were invented.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 12 --body-file /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yawoppong-krampah-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/a77ef331-d963-4153-904a-5fde226c3f3f/scratchpad/review12.md | tail -1","description":"Post review findings on #12"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":353,"cache_read_input_tokens":557904,"output_tokens":1949,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":122},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":353,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1949,"cache_read_input_tokens":557904,"cache_creation_input_tokens":353,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":353},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01NhS7w1M7PuA91RPFuVpnYz":{"command":"cd /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yawoppong-krampah-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/a77ef331-d963-4153-904a-5fde226c3f3f/scratchpad/review12.md <<'EOF'\n## T10 `/code-review` (#12): findings and how each was resolved\n\nWorking tree against `HEAD` (`fa94a01`), 447 tests passing. {"parentUuid":"e6b84995-1a0b-4a96-bbdb-3b6deb7df35a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfyXKncEHGBxgXa6wpZxW","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Both checks are built, reviewed and pushed as `75332b0`. A fresh clone passes 447 tests, the Stage 2 checker (22/22) and the Backends check. #12 was created before any code changed, and it closed at 03:23:23Z, after the review comment at 03:23:15Z. Both tags are unmoved: `mp2-final` is still `e3b0788` and `mp2-mvp` is still `06a3070`. I have not committed the report paragraph; it's below.\n\n**`cms deploy` test** (`tests/test_t10_deploy.py`, 6 tests)\n- **Setup:** it runs the real `cms publish`, then the real `cms deploy`, from a working repository whose `origin` is a temporary local bare repository. Git is limited to the `file` protocol, with global config nulled and redirect variables like `GIT_DIR` removed.\n- **No GitHub:** a test confirms git itself refuses an https remote (`transport 'https' not allowed`).\n- **What it checks:**\n  - Every exported file reaches `gh-pages` byte for byte, plus `.nojekyll`.\n  - No `main` is created, and a pre-existing `main` on the remote is left alone.\n  - A Draft never appears, including on a second deploy.\n  - An unpublished Post disappears on the next deploy.\n  - A missing `site/` is refused and nothing is pushed.\n\n**Backends check** (`scripts/check_backends.py`, 32 tests)\n- **Agreement:** it compares the README table, the ledger's provider and model columns, and every `Backend:` trailer in the history (the rubric's H6).\n- **ChatGPT:** it must appear in the README's own prose, and must never be a table row, a ledger provider or a trailer.\n- **Real repo:** it passes on the real repository, which has one Anthropic row, no trailers and an all-`anthropic` ledger. Negative controls cover each kind of disagreement.\n- **Hardening from review:** it also accepts trailers in any case or indented, rejects `Backend: <provider>` placeholders and a table hidden in a code block, keeps model ids with a `/` whole, and fails when `git log` is empty or unreadable.\n\n**Checks on the checks**\n- **Mutations:** I broke the code in 29 ways and 28 are caught, each by a named test. The one that isn't is adding `-f` to the push of the same `gh-pages` branch. It behaves identically unless someone else pushed in between, and no test sets that up, so I've recorded it as a gap rather than a pass.\n- **My first mutation run was invalid.** The script was untracked, so my restore step did nothing and the breakages piled up, making everything look caught. I restored the file and redid it with a copy-based restore. The honest run exposed four loose assertions, which I tightened.\n- **Reviewers:** they also found a dead filename assertion, a network test that could pass for the wrong reason, and the missing Git isolation. All are fixed and listed on #12.\n\n**Assessment (now version 2.3):** the totals are unchanged at 92 on `main` and 89 for the tag as it stands. The two tickets with an untested criterion are now covered, so E2's sampling risk drops from about 58% to about 33%. I kept E2 at 1 because T08 still has checklist statements that are not behaviour (Photo permission is confirmed by a leader, the author runs the release, no ASA owner is claimed). I won't add a test that only greps the wording; accepting one is your call.\n\n**Report section 3 paragraph, for your review** (saved in the scratchpad, not in the report):\n\n> **Why these steps, in this order.** I used the grill to make the decisions before any code, because the choices about who may do what had to be mine, not a guess by the model. The first prompt quoted in the README shows it: I decided that an Editor may update the Body of an existing Page, while the Admin controls creating, deleting, publishing and re-slugging Pages, and I wrote that this was my design choice for the ASA site, not something I had seen in WordPress. I broke the spec into eight tickets so that each session had one slice small enough to build and check, with its own acceptance criteria and a \"Blocked by\" line, instead of one large change I could not review. I used test-first development so that each ticket was judged by what the app does (what a signed-in Editor sees, which files `cms publish` writes) and not by how it is built. And I used an independent code review on every ticket because the AI both makes things up and misses things. The second prompt in the README is me removing the invented claim \"Today ASA has no site that does this\" before any ticket existed. Later reviews caught a form field that would have crashed on an unusual character and a browser check that would have passed on an error page.\n\nThe facts in it all check out against the repo (the two real prompts, the eight tickets, and the two review catches, both fixed before their commits). The reasons are the ones you gave me, not new ones. It's 228 words, which would push the report to roughly 1,150 words, past the manual's \"1–2 pages\". If you approve it I can fold it into section 3 and trim elsewhere to stay inside two pages. {"parentUuid":"264f3ef7-3945-4ad6-8917-549b832b668d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4631f74f-2fab-4f1b-b8ac-4453ed5da999","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GU2RNSwoN6aWh48fvGR3P8","type":"tool_result","content":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n\nYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08) plus a design ticket (T07b, opened after the redesign was built), and ends with 409 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements.** No separate Event type. The date, time, location and who can attend go in the Body.\n- **Editors can update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page can stay current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title on first save and then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** Content goes Live only after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, which I run myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer, more inviting one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught the unsupported claim while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed from `.env.example`: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association` because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. This was found before the clean-clone run. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug only showed when `uv` read the file. Claude Code then changed the test to run the seed through `uv --env-file` and quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\n- I used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, plus ChatGPT for planning and review assistance. The only models in the usage ledger are Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5. I also used the course manual and rubric and the mattpocock-skills plugin.\n- **ChatGPT.** I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n- I completed the grill, spec and ticket planning first. The transcripts show the sessions for T01 to T07 each began after `/clear` or with the `/implement` command; the work was test-first, and each ticket's code review was posted on its issue before it closed. T08 also began with `/clear`, but its transcript is written when the session ends, so it is not in the repository yet. The repair work for issue #11 happened in that same session, with no fresh context. T07b is the other exception: it was built in a resumed session after T07 was pushed, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign already existed. Its dependency on T07 was recorded afterwards, and #10 says so.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08) plus a design ticket (T07b, opened after the redesign was built), and ends with 409 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements.** No separate Event type. The date, time, location and who can attend go in the Body.\n- **Editors can update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page can stay current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title on first save and then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** Content goes Live only after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, which I run myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer, more inviting one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught the unsupported claim while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed from `.env.example`: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association` because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. This was found before the clean-clone run. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug only showed when `uv` read the file. Claude Code then changed the test to run the seed through `uv --env-file` and quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\n- I used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, plus ChatGPT for planning and review assistance. The only models in the usage ledger are Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5. I also used the course manual and rubric and the mattpocock-skills plugin.\n- **ChatGPT.** I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n- I completed the grill, spec and ticket planning first. The transcripts show the sessions for T01 to T07 each began after `/clear` or with the `/implement` command; the work was test-first, and each ticket's code review was posted on its issue before it closed. T08 also began with `/clear`, but its transcript is written when the session ends, so it is not in the repository yet. The repair work for issue #11 happened in that same session, with no fresh context. T07b is the other exception: it was built in a resumed session after T07 was pushed, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign already existed. Its dependency on T07 was recorded afterwards, and #10 says so.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. {"parentUuid":"d91efa20-eee1-4f00-b0e0-bb05749bf2b5","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4631f74f-2fab-4f1b-b8ac-4453ed5da999","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XY4JPxxJF7Rex59ij1kJmB","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n2\t\n3\tYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n4\t\n5\t## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n6\t\n7\tI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08) plus a design ticket (T07b, opened after the redesign was built), and ends with 409 tests.\n8\t\n9\tMy decisions in the grill:\n10\t\n11\t- **Ordinary Posts for announcements.** No separate Event type. The date, time, location and who can attend go in the Body.\n12\t- **Editors can update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page can stay current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n13\t- **Slugs come from the title on first save and then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n14\t- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n15\t- **Published is not Live.** Content goes Live only after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, which I run myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n16\t\n17\tAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer, more inviting one (T07b).\n18\t\n19\t## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n20\t\n21\t**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught the unsupported claim while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n22\t\n23\t**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed from `.env.example`: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association` because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. This was found before the clean-clone run. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug only showed when `uv` read the file. Claude Code then changed the test to run the seed through `uv --env-file` and quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n24\t\n25\t## 3. Resources and workflow\n26\t\n27\t- I used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, plus ChatGPT for planning and review assistance. The only models in the usage ledger are Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5. I also used the course manual and rubric and the mattpocock-skills plugin.\n28\t- **ChatGPT.** I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n29\t- I completed the grill, spec and ticket planning first. The transcripts show the sessions for T01 to T07 each began after `/clear` or with the `/implement` command; the work was test-first, and each ticket's code review was posted on its issue before it closed. T08 also began with `/clear`, but its transcript is written when the session ends, so it is not in the repository yet. The repair work for issue #11 happened in that same session, with no fresh context. T07b is the other exception: it was built in a resumed session after T07 was pushed, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign already existed. Its dependency on T07 was recorded afterwards, and #10 says so.\n30\t\n31\t## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n32\t\n33\tOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n34\t\n35\tI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n36\t\n37\t**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. A ledger snapshot taken on 2026-10-13 at 02:37 UTC (90 rows, the last at 02:30 UTC, from 16 sessions) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 points of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b (2 to 7 each). The T08 label (12 points) also covers the release, the submission checks and the rubric self-assessment, so it is not comparable with the other tickets. The repair work for issue #11 has its own label, T09, which shows 3 points so far; it continued after the snapshot, so the final figure will be higher.\n38\t\n39\tThese are coarse ledger measurements. The meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete: it has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, from 2026-09-29, and 10, 11 and 12, from 2026-10-01), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. I have not added or estimated rows for them, so the totals leave them out.\n40\t"}]},"uuid":"88ad2cf0-affc-49db-a573-f4a01922e559","timestamp":"2026-10-13T04:06:43.921Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_yaw-oppong-krampah_20261012.md","content":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n\nYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08) plus a design ticket (T07b, opened after the redesign was built), and ends with 409 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements.** No separate Event type. The date, time, location and who can attend go in the Body.\n- **Editors can update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page can stay current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title on first save and then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** Content goes Live only after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, which I run myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer, more inviting one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught the unsupported claim while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed from `.env.example`: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association` because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. This was found before the clean-clone run. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug only showed when `uv` read the file. Claude Code then changed the test to run the seed through `uv --env-file` and quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\n- I used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, plus ChatGPT for planning and review assistance. The only models in the usage ledger are Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5. I also used the course manual and rubric and the mattpocock-skills plugin.\n- **ChatGPT.** I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n- I completed the grill, spec and ticket planning first. The transcripts show the sessions for T01 to T07 each began after `/clear` or with the `/implement` command; the work was test-first, and each ticket's code review was posted on its issue before it closed. T08 also began with `/clear`, but its transcript is written when the session ends, so it is not in the repository yet. The repair work for issue #11 happened in that same session, with no fresh context. T07b is the other exception: it was built in a resumed session after T07 was pushed, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign already existed. Its dependency on T07 was recorded afterwards, and #10 says so.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b (2 to 7 each). The T08 label (12 points) also covers the release, the submission checks and the rubric self-assessment, so it is not comparable with the other tickets. The ledger is also incomplete: it has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, from 2026-09-29, and 10, 11 and 12, from 2026-10-01), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. {"parentUuid":"a50735f7-1155-48d8-80d4-6e62d311f345","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfyaQW1pvnfKEceZicGMN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01RHuT2JPiTR1K8WMMqzJ1g3","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_yaw-oppong-krampah_20261012.md","content":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n\nYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08), a design ticket (T07b) and later repairs, and ends with 447 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements**, with the date, time, location and who can attend in the Body. No separate Event type.\n- **Editors may update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page stays current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title once, then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** I run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught it while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, before the clean-clone run, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association`, because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug showed only when `uv` read the file. It changed the test to run the seed through `uv`, quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\nI used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, the course manual and rubric, and the mattpocock-skills plugin. I also used ChatGPT to understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so that rests on my own account.\n\nI used the grill to make the decisions myself: the first prompt quoted in the README is me choosing who may edit Pages, as my design choice and not something I saw in WordPress. I split the spec into eight tickets so each session had one slice small enough to check. Test-first development judged each ticket by what the app does, not how it is built. An independent review of every ticket caught mistakes, such as a form field that would crash on an unusual character; the second README prompt removes the invented claim before any ticket existed. T01 to T07 each began in a fresh session. T07b did not, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign existed. T08 and the repairs shared one session.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. A ledger snapshot on 2026-10-13 at 02:37 UTC (90 rows, 16 sessions) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b. T08 (12 points) also covers the release and submission checks, so it is not comparable, and repair work after the snapshot is not included.\n\nThese are coarse measurements: the meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete. It has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, 10, 11 and 12), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. I have not added or estimated rows for them, so the totals leave them out.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2790,"cache_read_input_tokens":572628,"output_tokens":1977,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":75},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2790,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1977,"cache_read_input_tokens":572628,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2790,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2790},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01RHuT2JPiTR1K8WMMqzJ1g3":{"file_path":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_yaw-oppong-krampah_20261012.md","content":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n\nYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08), a design ticket (T07b) and later repairs, and ends with 447 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements**, with the date, time, location and who can attend in the Body. No separate Event type.\n- **Editors may update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page stays current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title once, then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** I run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught it while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, before the clean-clone run, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association`, because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug showed only when `uv` read the file. It changed the test to run the seed through `uv`, quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\nI used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, the course manual and rubric, and the mattpocock-skills plugin. I also used ChatGPT to understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so that rests on my own account.\n\nI used the grill to make the decisions myself: the first prompt quoted in the README is me choosing who may edit Pages, as my design choice and not something I saw in WordPress. I split the spec into eight tickets so each session had one slice small enough to check. Test-first development judged each ticket by what the app does, not how it is built. An independent review of every ticket caught mistakes, such as a form field that would crash on an unusual character; the second README prompt removes the invented claim before any ticket existed. T01 to T07 each began in a fresh session. T07b did not, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign existed. T08 and the repairs shared one session.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. A ledger snapshot on 2026-10-13 at 02:37 UTC (90 rows, 16 sessions) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b. T08 (12 points) also covers the release and submission checks, so it is not comparable, and repair work after the snapshot is not included.\n\nThese are coarse measurements: the meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete. It has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, 10, 11 and 12), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. I have not added or estimated rows for them, so the totals leave them out.\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CfyaQVfVnEVmuRE9jdTEy","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"48f6537b-0b12-4f96-851e-fe146aefa5f8","timestamp":"2026-10-13T04:06:55.305Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a77ef331-d963-4153-904a-5fde226c3f3f","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08) plus a design ticket (T07b, opened after the redesign was built), and ends with 409 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements.** No separate Event type. The date, time, location and who can attend go in the Body.\n- **Editors can update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page can stay current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title on first save and then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** Content goes Live only after `cms publish` and `cms deploy`, which I run myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer, more inviting one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught the unsupported claim while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed from `.env.example`: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association` because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. This was found before the clean-clone run. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug only showed when `uv` read the file. Claude Code then changed the test to run the seed through `uv --env-file` and quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\n- I used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, plus ChatGPT for planning and review assistance. The only models in the usage ledger are Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5. I also used the course manual and rubric and the mattpocock-skills plugin.\n- **ChatGPT.** I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n- I completed the grill, spec and ticket planning first. The transcripts show the sessions for T01 to T07 each began after `/clear` or with the `/implement` command; the work was test-first, and each ticket's code review was posted on its issue before it closed. T08 also began with `/clear`, but its transcript is written when the session ends, so it is not in the repository yet. The repair work for issue #11 happened in that same session, with no fresh context. T07b is the other exception: it was built in a resumed session after T07 was pushed, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign already existed. Its dependency on T07 was recorded afterwards, and #10 says so.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. A ledger snapshot taken on 2026-10-13 at 02:37 UTC (90 rows, the last at 02:30 UTC, from 16 sessions) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 points of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b (2 to 7 each). The T08 label (12 points) also covers the release, the submission checks and the rubric self-assessment, so it is not comparable with the other tickets. The repair work for issue #11 has its own label, T09, which shows 3 points so far; it continued after the snapshot, so the final figure will be higher.\n\nThese are coarse ledger measurements. The meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket.
