{"parentUuid":"e060c973-90de-4fc3-8947-64e9ae4af6eb","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4631f74f-2fab-4f1b-b8ac-4453ed5da999","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GkBSZ8MkTmYLyvkAg8bagh","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n2\t\n3\tYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n4\t\n5\t## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n6\t\n7\tI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08), a design ticket (T07b) and later repairs, and ends with 447 tests.\n8\t\n9\tMy decisions in the grill:\n10\t\n11\t- **Ordinary Posts for announcements**, with the date, time, location and who can attend in the Body. No separate Event type.\n12\t- **Editors may update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page stays current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n13\t- **Slugs come from the title once, then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n14\t- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n15\t- **Published is not Live.** I run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n16\t\n17\tAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer one (T07b).\n18\t\n19\t## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n20\t\n21\t**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught it while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n22\t\n23\t**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, before the clean-clone run, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association`, because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug showed only when `uv` read the file. It changed the test to run the seed through `uv`, quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n24\t\n25\t## 3. Resources and workflow\n26\t\n27\tI used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, the course manual and rubric, and the mattpocock-skills plugin. I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n28\t\n29\tI used the grill so the decisions were mine: the first README prompt is me choosing who may edit Pages, and saying it was my design choice. Eight small tickets gave each session one slice to check, and test-first development judged what the app does, not how it is built. Independent review caught mistakes, such as a form field that would crash on an unusual character; the second README prompt removes the invented claim. T07b was built in a resumed session, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign existed.\n30\t\n31\t## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n32\t\n33\tOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n34\t\n35\tI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n36\t\n37\t**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. A ledger snapshot on 2026-10-13 at 02:37 UTC (90 rows, 16 sessions) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b. T08 (12 points) also covers the release and submission checks, so it is not comparable, and repair work after the snapshot is not included.\n38\t\n39\tThese are coarse measurements: the meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete. It has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, 10, 11 and 12), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. I have not added or estimated rows for them, so the totals leave them out.\n40\t"}]},"uuid":"5e0d80ac-c816-4bd2-b790-7dc0de33c9f7","timestamp":"2026-10-13T04:07:23.282Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_yaw-oppong-krampah_20261012.md","content":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n\nYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, before the clean-clone run, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association`, because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug showed only when `uv` read the file. It changed the test to run the seed through `uv`, quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\nI used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, the course manual and rubric, and the mattpocock-skills plugin. I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n\nI used the grill so the decisions were mine: the first README prompt is me choosing who may edit Pages, and saying it was my design choice. Eight small tickets gave each session one slice to check, and test-first development judged what the app does, not how it is built. Independent review caught mistakes, such as a form field that would crash on an unusual character; the second README prompt removes the invented claim. T07b was built in a resumed session, and its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign existed.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. A ledger snapshot on 2026-10-13 at 02:37 UTC (90 rows, 16 sessions) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b. T08 (12 points) also covers the release and submission checks, so it is not comparable, and repair work after the snapshot is not included.\n\nThese are coarse measurements: the meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete. It has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, 10, 11 and 12), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. I have not added or estimated rows for them, so the totals leave them out.\n\n---\n\n**Length**\n- **Whole file:** 800 words by `wc`, which counts headings, URLs and markdown symbols.\n- **Body text only:** 746 words, excluding headings and the author/URL line.\n- **Section 3:** 151 words without its heading, down from 189 with it.\n- **Pages:** I have not rendered it, so I'm not claiming it fits in two pages.\n\n**What changed**\n- **Section 3:** I removed the \"fresh context\" claims entirely instead of qualifying them. The ticket sessions, T08 and the repairs are no longer described, so the report no longer overclaims there. I kept the T07b admission, since it's a specific and costs one sentence.\n- **ChatGPT sentence:** kept verbatim, with the note that no ChatGPT conversation is saved in the repo.\n- **Test count:** now 447, which I verified on the fresh clone of `75332b0`; it was 409 before.\n- **`.env.example` paragraph:** it still says the defect was found before the clean-clone run.\n- **Dropped:** a few repeated or minor sentences, such as the \"each ticket's review was posted before it closed\" detail (in the issues and the README) and the \"(T07b, opened after the redesign was built)\" aside (now said once, in section 3).\n\n**Facts checked against the repo**\n- **Ledger snapshot:** the committed ledger at the commit that included it (`afd69bd`) has exactly 90 rows and 16 sessions, matching the report. The working-tree ledger has since grown to 96 rows, so the report correctly cites the committed snapshot.\n- **Budget figures:** the 53 and 6 totals and the per-stage comparisons come from that snapshot.\n- **Review example:** the \"form field that would crash on an unusual character\" is the `post_id` hidden field in the Event details hint, fixed before the T08 commit.\n\n**Two things you might want to change**\n- The \"later repairs\" in section 1 is vague on purpose. I can name #11 and #12 if you'd rather.\n- I did not carry over the \"T08 transcript is not in the repository yet\" caveat or the \"fresh context\" qualification. {"parentUuid":"d07df1bb-6ae6-45a1-9b5b-3ffe43f5efae","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ee58085c-b7d9-446b-9755-39023cee7a86","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018VJHURLHkSfmfE1aXiii9L","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n2\t\n3\tYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n4\t\n5\t## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n6\t\n7\tI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08), a design ticket (T07b) and the later repairs in issues #11 and #12, and ends with 447 tests.\n8\t\n9\tMy decisions in the grill:\n10\t\n11\t- **Ordinary Posts for announcements**, with the date, time, location and who can attend in the Body. No separate Event type.\n12\t- **Editors may update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page stays current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n13\t- **Slugs come from the title once, then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n14\t- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n15\t- **Published is not Live.** I run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n16\t\n17\tAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer one (T07b).\n18\t\n19\t## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n20\t\n21\t**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught it while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n22\t\n23\t**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, before the clean-clone run, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association`, because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug showed only when `uv` read the file. It changed the test to run the seed through `uv`, quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n24\t\n25\t## 3. Resources and workflow\n26\t\n27\tI used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, the course manual and rubric, and the mattpocock-skills plugin. I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n28\t\n29\tI used the grill so the decisions were mine: the first README prompt is me choosing who may edit Pages. Eight small tickets gave each session one slice to check, and test-first development judged what the app does, not how it is built. Independent review caught mistakes, such as a form field that would crash on an unusual character; the second README prompt removes the invented claim. The eight core tickets used fresh implementation contexts; the later design follow-up continued in an existing session. Its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign existed.\n30\t\n31\t## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n32\t\n33\tOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n34\t\n35\tI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n36\t\n37\t**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. The ledger as committed on 2026-10-13 (snapshot taken at 02:37 UTC, 90 rows, 16 sessions, unchanged since) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b. T08 (12 points) also covers the release and submission checks, so it is not comparable, and work after the snapshot is not in the ledger.\n38\t\n39\tThese are coarse measurements: the meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete. As of that snapshot it has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, 10, 11 and 12), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. I have not added or estimated rows for them, so the totals leave them out.\n40\t"}]},"uuid":"3cfe75ff-7619-4358-965c-c038ef77bc99","timestamp":"2026-10-13T04:23:04.431Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_yaw-oppong-krampah_20261012.md","content":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n\nYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08), a design ticket (T07b) and the later repairs in issues #11 and #12, and ends with 447 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements**, with the date, time, location and who can attend in the Body. No separate Event type.\n- **Editors may update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page stays current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title once, then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** I run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught it while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, before the clean-clone run, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association`, because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug showed only when `uv` read the file. It changed the test to run the seed through `uv`, quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\nI used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, the course manual and rubric, and the mattpocock-skills plugin. I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n\nI used the grill so the decisions were mine: the first README prompt is me choosing who may edit Pages. Eight small tickets gave each session one slice to check, and test-first development judged what the app does, not how it is built. Independent review caught mistakes, such as a form field that would crash on an unusual character; the second README prompt removes the invented claim. The eight core tickets used fresh implementation contexts; the later design follow-up continued in an existing session. Its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign existed.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. The ledger as committed on 2026-10-13 (snapshot taken at 02:37 UTC, 90 rows, 16 sessions, unchanged since) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b. T08 (12 points) also covers the release and submission checks, so it is not comparable, and work after the snapshot is not in the ledger.\n\nThese are coarse measurements: the meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete. As of that snapshot it has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, 10, 11 and 12), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%. I have not added or estimated rows for them, so the totals leave them out.\n","numLines":40,"startLine":1,"totalLines":40}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d07df1bb-6ae6-45a1-9b5b-3ffe43f5efae","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a77ef331-d963-4153-904a-5fde226c3f3f","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"498ec91c-874e-4ada-af74-6d8e09827bbc","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfybekVySLq8CSeqWYrAV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Both files are edited in the working tree and nothing is committed or staged. Here is the complete final report, then the score and the transcript check.\n\n---\n\n# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: report\n\nYaw Oppong-Krampah · repo https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms · Live site https://yawoppongkrampah-hub.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\n## 1. What I built, and the decisions that were mine\n\nI built a small CMS for the African Student Association (ASA) at Kenyon. A local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite), never on the public internet, lets an Admin and Editors write Posts and Pages. `cms publish` turns only Published content into plain HTML, and `cms deploy` pushes it to GitHub Pages. The work ran as eight tickets (T01 to T08), a design ticket (T07b) and the later repairs in issues #11 and #12, and ends with 447 tests.\n\nMy decisions in the grill:\n\n- **Ordinary Posts for announcements**, with the date, time, location and who can attend in the Body. No separate Event type.\n- **Editors may update the Body of an existing Page**, so the Photos page stays current. Admins control Page structure and users.\n- **Slugs come from the title once, then stay put**, so shared links keep working.\n- **Accounts are deactivated, never deleted**, and bylines use a public Display name.\n- **Published is not Live.** I run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` myself from my laptop (`docs/release-checklist.md`).\n\nAfter the first public design looked sparse, I asked for a warmer one (T07b).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and what caught it\n\n**The invented claim.** The model's first spec draft said \"Today ASA has no site that does this.\" I had not supplied that fact, and the client brief does not say it. With ChatGPT's help, I caught it while reviewing issue #1 and asked Claude Code to remove it before creating tickets. The same edit changed \"upcoming events\" to \"event announcements\".\n\n**The `.env.example` defect.** While setting up the T08 demo, before the clean-clone run, Claude Code found that the README's setup failed: `uv` could not parse `CMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association`, because the multi-word value was not quoted. The unquoted style came from the starter template, and my own `.env` had quotes, so I had never hit it. Claude Code's first seed test parsed the file by hand and passed anyway; the bug showed only when `uv` read the file. It changed the test to run the seed through `uv`, quoted the line, and a fresh clone signed in as both roles.\n\n## 3. Resources and workflow\n\nI used Claude Code with Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5, the course manual and rubric, and the mattpocock-skills plugin. I also used ChatGPT to help me understand the assignment, think through CMS decisions, review Claude Code's output, and refine the website design and submission steps. No ChatGPT conversation is saved in this repository, so this rests on my own account.\n\nI used the grill so the decisions were mine: the first README prompt is me choosing who may edit Pages. Eight small tickets gave each session one slice to check, and test-first development judged what the app does, not how it is built. Independent review caught mistakes, such as a form field that would crash on an unusual character; the second README prompt removes the invented claim. The eight core tickets used fresh implementation contexts; the later design follow-up continued in an existing session. Its issue (#10) was opened after the redesign existed.\n\n## 4. What I would add next, and what the budget data says\n\nOne limitation I would change is event scheduling. I chose ordinary Posts to keep the project manageable, but this means the site cannot automatically separate upcoming events from past ones. Adding an event-date field would make the announcements more useful.\n\nI would also end sessions properly. Sessions are signed cookies with no server-side record, so a copied cookie works for 8 hours or until the account is Deactivated, and a password reset does not end sessions already signed in. I accepted this for the demo, because the console only runs on my laptop, and wrote it into the release checklist.\n\n**Budget.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` estimated about 340% of one 5-hour window. The ledger as committed on 2026-10-13 (snapshot taken at 02:37 UTC, 90 rows, 16 sessions, unchanged since) shows about 53 percentage points of 5-hour meter increase and 6 of weekly increase (`usage_report.py --remaining 0`). Planned against recorded: `/grill` 15 vs 2, `/to-spec` 10 vs 1, `/to-tickets` 10 vs 3, and 28 per ticket for implementation plus review vs 4 on average for T01 to T07b. T08 (12 points) also covers the release and submission checks, so it is not comparable, and work after the snapshot is not in the ledger.\n\nThese are coarse measurements: the meters move in whole percentage points, and implementation and review share one number per ticket. The ledger is also incomplete. As of that snapshot it has no rows for four of the 19 transcript sessions (04, 10, 11 and 12), so it covers 15 of 19, or 79%.
